title: Cleansing is gradual; perfect holiness grows (2 Cor 7; Rev 22)
source_text: XVI. Porro ista a peccatis purgatio & emundatio tota simul & semel non fit, sed sensim & per gradus varios promovetur. Unde est quod Apostolus illos ipsos quos supponit gratiae Christi participes, & quorum numero ipse se includit, hortatur ut se magis ac magis mundent, & perficiant sanctificationem. Has ergo, inquit, habentes promissiones, charissimi, mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis & spiritus, sanctificationem perficientes in timore Dei. 2 Cor. 7. Quo spectat illud Apocalypseos, Qui justus est justificetur adhuc; & sanctus est sanctificetur adhuc. Apoc. 22.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover that purgation and cleansing from sins does not happen all at once and once for all, but is advanced gradually and through various degrees. Hence it is that the Apostle exhorts those very ones whom he assumes to be sharers of Christ's grace, and in whose number he includes himself, to cleanse themselves more and more and perfect sanctification. Having therefore these promises, beloved, he says, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God (2 Corinthians 7). To which looks that of the Apocalypse: Let him who is righteous be justified still; and he who is holy be sanctified still (Revelation 22).
pass_b_english: Cleansing is not once-for-all total; it advances by degrees.
Paul urges sharers of grace to perfect sanctification (2 Corinthians 7); Revelation 22: the righteous and holy still grow.
